statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail. It satisfies len(r) = 2. For every i64 value p, p occurs in r[0] if and only if p occurs in some match entry and p has no loss, i.e. (exists i with 0 <= i < len(matches) and (matches[i][0] = p or matches[i][1] = p)) and (there is no j with 0 <= j < len(matches) and matches[j][1] = p). For every i64 value p, p occurs in r[1] if and only if p occurs in some match entry and p has exactly one loss, i.e. (exists i with 0 <= i < len(matches) and (matches[i][0] = p or matches[i][1] = p)) and (there is exactly one j with 0 <= j < len(matches) and matches[j][1] = p). Finally, for each b in {0,1}, r[b] is strictly increasing: for all indices j,k with 0 <= j < k < len(r[b]), r[b][j] < r[b][k]. Here 'p occurs in r[b]' means there exists t with 0 <= t < len(r[b]) and r[b][t] = p.
